# Tus-DotNetClient

Source: https://github.com/spookylsm/tus-dotnetclient/blob/main/README.md

# Tus-DotNetClient

.NET client for the [tus.io](http://tus.io/) resumable upload protocol.

## Features

- Supports tus v1.0.0
- Protocol extensions supported: Creation, Termination
- Resumable uploads based on server-reported offsets
- Upload and download progress events
- Proxy support through `TusClient.Proxy`

## Usage

```c#
var file = new FileInfo(@"path/to/file.ext");
var client = new TusClient();

var metadata = new[]
{
    ("filename", file.Name),
    ("contentType", "application/octet-stream")
};

var fileUrl = await client.CreateAsync(Address, file.Length, metadata);
await client.UploadAsync(fileUrl, file, chunkSize: 5D);
```

### Progress updates

`UploadAsync` and `DownloadAsync` return `TusOperation<T>`, which exposes a `Progressed` event. The operation will not start until the returned object is awaited.

Store the return object in a variable and subscribe to the event before awaiting it.

```c#
var file = new FileInfo(@"path/to/file.ext");
var client = new TusClient();
var fileUrl = await client.CreateAsync(Address, file);
var uploadOperation = client.UploadAsync(fileUrl, file, chunkSize: 5D);

uploadOperation.Progressed += (transferred, total) =>
    System.Diagnostics.Debug.WriteLine($"Progress: {transferred}/{total}");

await uploadOperation;
```

### Custom headers and proxy

```c#
var client = new TusClient
{
    Proxy = new WebProxy("http://proxy:8080")
};

client.AdditionalHeaders.Add("Authorization", "Bearer <token>");
```

## Development

- Build: `dotnet build TusDotNetClient.sln -c Release`
- Test: `dotnet test tests/TusDotNetClientTests/TusDotNetClientTests.csproj -c Release`
- Pack: `dotnet pack src/TusDotNetClient/TusDotNetClient.csproj -c Release -p:Version=3.0.1`

Release versions are computed in GitHub Actions from the latest `v*` tag. Set `RELEASE_MAJOR` and `RELEASE_MINOR` in `.github/workflows/release_v1.yml`, and the pipeline will publish the next patch in that series automatically.

The test project is self-contained and runs against an in-process test server; it does not require an external `tusd` binary.
